chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Musa ibn Jaʿfar, from Abi Jaʿfar, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Luʾluʾi, from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn Faḍḍal, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Aba ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام saying: “Everything from your salat and your taharah that has already passed, then you remember it afterward by recollection, let it pass, and there is no repetition upon you regarding it.”

key_terms.إِعَادَةَ: repetition or performing the act again
key_terms.تَذَكُّرًا: recollection afterward, remembering something after the act has passed
key_terms.صَلَاتِكَ: your salat (prayer), the ritual prayer already performed
key_terms.طَهُورِكَ: your taharah, meaning your state or act of ritual purification
key_terms.فَأَمْضِهِ: then let it pass; continue without reopening the matter

ai.seo_question: If I remember a possible mistake in my salat or wudu after finishing, do I have to repeat it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning doubt or recollection after completing acts such as salat and taharah. If a person remembers a past matter after it has already passed, he should proceed and is not required to repeat it.
